generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the grass base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the grass program gave as defaults until then.

traits.note: Plants of the World Online's account of the family, with Go Botany, as search results quote them (the pages themselves were not read): flowers actinomorphic; perianth segments 6 in 2 whorls (rarely 3), usually glumaceous; stamens 6 or 3, free; ovary superior, of 3 united carpels, stigmas 3.

traits.leaf_division.note: Hutchinson (vol. 2, 2nd ed., 1959), family 406 Juncaceae: leaves mostly in a basal tuft, cylindrical to flat and grass-like, mostly linear or thread-like, or only a sheath; flowers bisexual, or unisexual on separate plants; fruit a dry capsule opening along its cells.

traits.life_span.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Juncaceae: the herbs' life form (character 21), coded usually perennial, sometimes annual. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 261, 263, family Juncaceae: phyllotaxis pattern tristichous (rarely distichous), usually; read as {"tristichous": "usually"}.

traits.leaf_venation.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 261, 263, family Juncaceae: leaf venation parallel; read as "parallel".

traits.inflorescence.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 261, 263, family Juncaceae: inflorescence solitary or cyme (or compound of cymes, glomerules or heads); read as {"cyme": "often", "solitary": "often"}.

traits.rosette.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 261, 263, family Juncaceae: rosette basal (leaves mostly basal), usually; read as {"basal": "usually"}.

traits.rhizome_habit.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 261, 263, family Juncaceae: rhizome habit short_creeping (perennials rhizomatous), usually; read as {"short_creeping": "usually"}.
